html:
Physicist and chemist, born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw in 1867, who worked in Paris. She discovered polonium and radium and was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.

Warsaw was then under Russian rule, and women could not attend university. She studied in secret and in 1891 moved to Paris, where she studied physics at the Sorbonne. She married Pierre Curie.

Inspired by Henri Becquerel's discovery of rays from uranium, she studied the new effect and named it radioactivity. Working with tonnes of uranium ore waste from Joachimsthal in Bohemia, the Curies found two new elements in 1898: polonium, named after her homeland Poland, and radium.

  • 1903: Nobel Prize in Physics, shared with Pierre and Becquerel.
  • 1906: Pierre was killed in a street accident; she took over his chair, the first woman professor at the University of Paris.
  • 1911: Nobel Prize in Chemistry, alone.

She died in 1934 of a blood disease caused by long exposure to radiation. Her daughter Irène also won a Nobel Prize.
sum: Physicist and chemist, born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw in 1867, who worked in Paris. She discovered polonium and radium and was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.
